nodes.summary: The canonical factor is a preimage: `B (C x) = A x`.
nodes.title: Douglas factor gives a preimage under B

nodes.summary: The canonical factor is continuous, by the (sequential) closed graph theorem: if `u n → x` and `C (u n) → y`, then `y ∈ (ker B)ᗮ` (the orthogonal complement is closed) and `B y = A x` (continuity of `A` and `B`), so `y = C x` by uniqueness of the preimage in `(ker B)ᗮ`.
nodes.title: Continuity of the Douglas factor via the closed graph theorem

nodes.summary: The canonical factor is the unique operator with the two defining properties.
nodes.title: Uniqueness of the Douglas factor

nodes.summary: The defining properties of the chosen preimage.
nodes.title: Defining properties of the Douglas preimage

nodes.summary: The underlying function of the canonical factor: the chosen preimage of `A x` in `(ker B)ᗮ`.
nodes.title: Underlying function of the Douglas factor

nodes.summary: The canonical factor as a linear map.
nodes.title: Douglas factor as a linear map

nodes.summary: The canonical factor lands in `(ker B)ᗮ`.
nodes.title: Douglas factor takes values in the kernel's orthogonal complement

nodes.summary: The canonical factor in Douglas' lemma: for `x : E`, the unique element of `(ker B)ᗮ` mapped by `B` to `A x`.
nodes.title: Canonical factor in Douglas' lemma
Douglas factor factors A through B

nodes.summary: Two points of `(ker B)ᗮ` with the same image under `B` are equal, since their difference lies in `ker B ∩ (ker B)ᗮ`.
nodes.title: Injectivity of an operator on the orthogonal complement of its kernel

nodes.summary: Douglas' lemma, factorization form with a norm bound: majorization with constant `c` yields a factor `C` with `A = B ∘L C` and `‖C‖ ≤ c`.
nodes.title: Douglas' lemma: majorization gives a norm-bounded factor

nodes.summary: If `A.range ≤ B.range`, every `A x` has a preimage under `B` in `(ker B)ᗮ`.
nodes.title: Preimages in the orthogonal complement of the kernel under range inclusion

nodes.summary: Douglas' lemma, majorization form: majorization holds iff `A` factors through `B`.
nodes.title: Douglas' lemma: majorization iff factorization

nodes.summary: If `A = B ∘L C`, then majorization holds with constant `‖C‖`.
nodes.title: Factorization implies majorization

nodes.summary: Douglas' lemma, range form: `A.range ≤ B.range` iff `A = B ∘L C` for some bounded `C`.
nodes.title: Douglas' lemma: range inclusion iff factorization

nodes.summary: Douglas' lemma, range/majorization form: `A.range ≤ B.range` iff majorization holds.
nodes.title: Douglas' lemma: range inclusion iff majorization

can_prove.label: ready to prove
can_prove.meaning: Statement is in Lean and nothing it needs is blocked, so the proof can start.

can_state.label: ready to state
can_state.meaning: Everything its statement uses is in Lean, so the statement can be written in Lean.

conditional.label: conditionally proved
conditional.meaning: Proof compiles, but rests on an open statement without a recorded Lean proof.

fully_proved.label: fully proved
fully_proved.meaning: Proved, and every prerequisite is fully proved too.

inventory_checked.label: inventory checked
inventory_checked.meaning: Module inventory checked in full; it records inspection, not a mathematical proof.

inventory_pending.label: inventory pending
inventory_pending.meaning: Module inventory not yet checked in full; it records inspection, not a mathematical proof.

not_ready.label: not ready
not_ready.meaning: Needs more blueprint work before it can be attempted.

proved.label: proved
proved.meaning: Proof compiles, but something it rests on is not finished.

stated.label: statement formalized
stated.meaning: Statement is in Lean; the proof is not.
